marina: quick heads-up — during the gemmaX int4 bring-up i see a reproducible quality regression on long-context QA. answers start to drift after ~2048 tokens. pattern looks like token misalignment + rope phase wrap 

marina: minimal repro attached (python). observed logits mismatch between fp16 baseline and int4 quant: small peak shifts across vocabulary that correlate with token id offsets in the tail.

marina: snippets:
```python
# run: python repro.py --model gemmaX --quant int4 --max_len 4096
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
# ... load tokenizer, model, compare logits
print('first ids', ids[:20])
print('slice logits', logits[:, -5:])
```

marina: example log (fp16 vs int4):
```
context_len=2100 prompt_len=1800
fp16_top1: "Paris" (token id 3452)
int4_top1: "Pari" (token id 3451)  <-- off by one on repeated spans
```

ow: curious if this is a tokenizer->vocab alias or a roPE headwise wrap issue. i dumped token ids around the boundary and saw repeated patterns where ids shift by +1 for ~64 tokens, then resync. :thinking_face:

ow: repro gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/commit/8a4a2c (script + sample seeds)

ow: owen, any chance this rings a bell with the kv-cache index math changes from last quarter?

ow: owen: odd — reminds me of the kv index fence bug we fixed for llama3 where long-context sharded caches missed a modulus. could be either: tokenizer off-by-one mapping or kvcache offset wrap. do you have id diffs?

marina: pasted a small diff of ids around 2038..2052 in the gist; there is a contiguous block where every id is -1 compared to fp16 baseline, then it flips to +1 later. not random.

sasha: can you dump the rotary phase for those positions? gemmaX uses per-head phase scaling that can cause aliasing when position index is off by headwise_stride. if kvcache indexing uses global position vs per-shard pos we can get a phase mismatch that looks like token shifts at decode time.

marina: good call. i dumped cos/sin vectors and saw a phase discontinuity exactly where the id drift starts. means position used by rotary != tokenizer position.

sam: short repro i ran locally — used this CLI:
```
./eval_run --model gemmaX --tokens 4096 --quant int4 --seed 42 --dump-ids out.ids
python compare_ids.py out.ids baseline.ids
```

sam: my quick experiment: forcing tokenizer to use incremental positions (instead of absolute) removed the drift for the int4 run. so it's definitely a positional/kv alignment issue, not vocab mismap. :eyes:

kevin: that matches a hypothesis: quant path uses a different decode loop that reinitializes position counters per micro-batch. the asm kernels we use for int4 have a micro-batching optimization that increments a local pos pointer and then writes back with a base offset. if that base is off by one for certain micro-batches you'll see the exact phase slip.

kevin: simple mitigation: when building the kv-cache index, use the global decode_step counter instead of microbatch_local and assert continuity across shards. adding that assertion caught a bug in my local run.

marina: great — can someone open a tiny PR with the assert+fallback? i'll run the int4 canary after.

kevin: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/842 — adds assert and fallback to global decode_step for int4 kernels.

deploy-bot: canary job started for PR #842 (job id: 987). running eval suite: long-context-qa, squad, rouge-smoke. ETA ~25m. :rocket:

marina: running the repro against that branch now. will post numbers shortly.

marina: quick results from canary: int4 top1 accuracy on long-qa improved from 72.3% -> 80.9% (baseline fp16 81.4%). drift gone for tested seeds.

sam: nice. any perf regress?

kevin: negligible perf cost — the assert is only on init path and the fallback is identical in steady state.

marina: i'll merge once we have a short postmortem and add an eval check to catch this class of misalignment (compare cos/sin continuity and kvcache positions).

marina: follow-up items:
- add small unit that verifies decode_step monotonicity across microbatches on int paths
- add tokenizer sanity check when loading shared vocab maps (edge cases with sentinel/pad aliases)
- add an automatic smoke eval for 4k+ contexts on PRs that touch kernel or kvcache code

marina: thanks all — saved us from a nasty production regression. :clap:
